For the Bosniak people this religious institution was protected because it would have been a sin if it had been damaged. This concerns the Bosniak people from the area I come from. I know that later on, part of the military police battalion of 20 the 3rd Corps were sent there and they had the same task and for a certain 21 period of time, together with the members of the military police from the 22 306th,they provided security for the monastery and they protected it from 23 whoever could launch and attack, and kept it intact.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that those combat operations continued and that around the 12th of June the command met. Did you notice that in the wider area Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of the Bila Valley there were looting incidents? Did you notice that any buildings were being torched? Who was doing this? Who was responsible for that area? And what exactly did the 306th do in order to discover who the perpetrators were and to punish them?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first stages of combat and afterwards, a small number of buildings were set on fire. Guca Gora and the villages which are closer to the established line were constantly under fire. There was constant combat action and buildings were set on fire, because shells were used and various types of ammunition. But when conditions were being created to go to Zenica via Gostunj, when the Travnik-Zenica road was being opened, this became a transit road. And on a daily basis thousands of refugees, thousands of travellers took that road and it was very difficult to control the situation. I think that almost everyone participated in the looting from the civilian population. I don't know who exactly participated in the looting. It couldn't be controlled because there were refugees from Travnik, from Zenica. There was movement from all areas in that territory. The protection of buildings and territory was the responsibility of the military police. The assistant for security could say more about this because he had to take these measures. I was involved in combat operations because there were counterattacked that were launched on a daily basis. When there's a combat operation, you have the attack and a counterattack. That's always the case so it's necessary to organise the defence. As far as I know, the 306th Brigade engaged the military police for protection. This was to the extent they had this capacity. There was the Mosor police station, which controlled that part of the territory and they were supposed to protect that part of the territory because combat units were engaged in combat action. And as far as I know the civilian protection staff from that area formed some kind of units to provide protection for the livestock and for land that had been abandoned. They also formed the unit to provide security for buildings abandoned by Croats. And attempts were also made -- according to a task assigned by the War Presidency, the municipal staff of civilian protection formed commissions in local communes, and this was -- these were commissions that had to deal with refugees entering abandoned Croatian houses that had been abandoned because they thought this was the only way of protecting these houses. So when people moved into these houses it was sometimes recorded so that the person moving into a house could be held responsible for the house. But there were also cases of people moving into these houses on their own initiative.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that your military police platoon also had the task of preventing looting and punishing looting by individuals or punishing individuals who might torch buildings. The military police of the 306th Brigade had responsibility over whom? Over all those thousands of people who were passing through? What was its field of competence?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was saying a minute ago, I said that the units of the command of the military police was only responsible for its own unit, for its subordinates, not for the civilian population because as I said there's the police station in Travnik responsible for the civilians and there are police stations in the field responsible for the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before this Tribunal, we have heard a lot about the concept of zone of responsibility. Could you tell us, since you are of the 306th Brigade which was deployed in the manner that you have indicated, could you tell us how the zone of responsibility of your brigade was determined. Were you responsible for all the territory that you have indicated on the map here?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps the orders could be examined, too, but there were orders from the corps command in which zones of responsibility were determined, in the sense of these zones being zones in which combat operations were conducted. The BH army task and the 306th Brigade task was to defend the current line that they were holding against the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor. They were to plan combat to liberate temporarily occupied territory. To that effect, the zone was determined with a left and right border. These borders were determined in this way: There was one point in the depth, there was one point at the demarcation line of the forces itself, and the other points were in the depth of the enemy's territory, or rather in the depth of the temporarily occupied territory, because that was a zone in which we were to engage in combat. We were to hold the current line and advance the line because we had to liberate the temporarily occupied territory. So the 306th had the left and right border and there was a zone of responsibility which was determined on the basis of the depth.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's a little clearer to me now. But let's now go back to the military police and the measures that they took. Was the military police in contact with the chief of staff or the commander?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the chief of staff, but in the end the commander is in command of everyone. But professionally speaking, they are linked to the chief of security, not the chief of staff. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From those meetings of the command that you must have had at regular intervals, can you tell me whether you became aware of the fact that there were orders about the protection of civilian facilities? Did your commander issue orders that should be taken against perpetrators? And do you know whether the commander of the 306th Brigade took any measures, and if so which measures did they take?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the orders from the superior command are concerned and relaying these orders to subordinates, I already said that when the 306th was being formed we started receiving such orders. I think this started at the beginning of 1993 and such orders from the superior command arrived very frequently. I know that they arrived again in February and then I think in April, in June on a number of occasions. And we relayed these orders to our subordinates and requests were made for measures to be taken. I didn't draft those orders myself. This was the task of the chief of security on the whole, but I am aware of this being done.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you took care of soldiers who could engage in combat, in the course of your duties did you become aware of the fact that there were any members of the 306th Brigade who were -- against whom disciplinary measures were taken? Were any members reported were having committed crimes? And were drastic measures ever taken against members of your brigade, that is, in order to punish looting, torching, or rather to prevent such acts?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm aware of this because sometimes I had problems as far as the rotation of units is concerned. That is because our detention unit was awful full and we didn't have any units to take over a shift. So sometimes I suggested that the commander release some detainees so that we could replenish the line, because when in conflict with the HVO we had an entire line, we had a very long line. We had a newly opened line in the direction of the HVO. So there was an immense burden on the men. And at meetings a lot was said about measures taken, about Prosecutions instituted. There were criminal reports as well and disciplinary measures were often taken and the commander would often given men up to two months' prison sentence. Men from the military battalion also did this. I don't know which acts this concerned. It was for acts of disobedience, et cetera. But I know that everything was done to make sure that the units behaved according to the code of conduct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Given the gravity of the problem and given all the civilians and soldiers, given the scale on which these acts were committed, did the corps command make additional efforts to reinforce the teams involved in investigations and the teams involved in disciplining men? Were any new units formed? And did the command have control over the situation in the territory of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the Travnik-Zenica road was opened, when it was possible to examine the situation, then in the command, in the operations group --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which operations group?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosanska Krajina Operations Group. It was said it was essential to reinforce the military police in order to carry out control because the soldiers who left the lines and went home because they weren't staying in barracks. In such cases it was possible for such soldiers to also commit illegal acts, and I am aware of this because I received the order to send from the 306th Brigade a group of five to seven armed MPs from our military police platoon. We were to send them to the company of the military police of the Bosanska Krajina OG. Military police company in the Bosanska Krajina OG was formed. We sent five armed members there, but we were then told that the MP company would be a sort of centre where MPs would be trained in order to perform the 11 duties of military policemen and then they would be sent back to their units, 12 so that we could have well-trained military policemen in our units. In other 13 words, an MP company was formed within the Bosanska Krajina OG was formed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, now that I am approaching the end of my examination, I would like to show you the other documents contained in your binder. They are in part entitled "Other Documents." And could we have a look together at those documents. Then you could briefly tell us whether you are familiar with these documents and you could tell us what the documents are about.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, which documents are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The documents entitled "Other Documents." You can see the title "Other Documents" on a white sheet of paper.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know English. Does it say "O-t-h-e-r"?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell me whether you are familiar with document number 1? Can you recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th of August, 1992, I was in the Territorial Defence municipal staff and I am familiar with this document because the 1st Krajina Battalion was formed in Travnik on the basis of an order. It was to be a unit subordinate to the municipal defence staff in Travnik. And when we were issuing orders, planning combat, we were to provide this 1st Battalion with orders, too. But later this battalion moved to the district municipal staff in Zenica -- the district Territorial Defence staff in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you have a look at document number 2, please.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the first documents from the 3rd Corps command. I have perhaps already mentioned this. It is an order that has to do with preventing the capturing of civilians, the burning of property, and looting. I said -- as I have already said, there were numerous such documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you have a look at document number 3. Defence number for this document is 0711.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document which shows how the 306th Mountain Brigade acted when they received orders from their superior command in relation to implementing the order to respect international humanitarian law. In this case it has to do with capturing civilians, torching buildings, looting incidents, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at document number 4. Defence number 0913. Did your brigade receive this document?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an order from the 3rd Corps command. And on the basis of the stamp you can see it was received by the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please have a look at the documents under "Exhibits," E-x-h-i-b-i-t-s. And have a look at the part entitled "DH Exhibits." Let me explain. This is already admitted into evidence. DH exhibits means that the document has been admitted into evidence and DH means -- well, I won't go into this. But have a look at document number 1. It's dated 29th of May, 1993. It's a document from the corps. And since it says: "In the area of the municipality of Travnik" -- have a look what it says there under that title and tell me whether you are familiar with the events that occurred during that period of time. What exactly do you know about these events?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day I was in Travnik, because on the 20th -- the 27th of May I left the brigade command, I arrived in Travnik, and at the checkpoint in Gostunj I was stopped. My computer was taken from me, or rather the brigade command's computer was taken away and I was not able to return to my command. The sniper activity, et cetera, I myself experienced this in the town. And when it says that the road Travnik-Guca Gora-Han Bila is blocked -- well, I wasn't able to return. I'm familiar with the document and the information contained was on the basis of our reports, either from the 306th or from units in Travnik, the --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With regard to that computer, you said that it was taken away from you in May. Can you tell us whether this computer was a device which made it possible for the 306th to have packet communications with the superior command. Is that the communications device in question?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that computer was one we received around the 10th of May. We were very happy about it because we thought we would have communications with our superior command, we would have packet communications with our superior command. And initially there were probably some problems with the computer, and in order to solve these problems we had to take the computer to Travnik so that it could be modified or something like that, so that we could use it. So we didn't even have it for ten days. It didn't last for long. It was supposed to be used for packet communications with our superior command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the next document, please, under number 2. In the right-hand corner it says DH157/12. Are the facts related this document facts that you are personally familiar with?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can say for sure is I was in Krpeljici and on that day there was a multiple rocket launcher which was in action. There was shooting but I don't know who was shooting in the Lasva Valley, so I couldn't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you have a look at document number 3. This is Defence's document. I think it's 280. Let me check -- I apologise. It's 270. DH270. Please have a look at the document. Could you tell me, are you familiar with this event? Did you personally witness the event related in this document?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of my duties and when investigating the activities of the subordinate units, an operative officer visited the 306th Brigade and the positions of its units. So this is a normal way to report to the corps commander about the situation in the units. And as the chief of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. staff of the 306th Brigade together with that operations officer from the corps command, I visited the lines, I visited the units. And this is a report drafted by this operations officer from the corps command. And it was for us, too, in order to inform us of what he observed. The task was to deal with all the weaknesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any time point out to the member of the command of the 3rd Corps the problems you were having with foreigners in your area? And were you in a position that see the facilities, the buildings, where these foreigners were located?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I informed this operations officer from the 3rd Corps command about the problems caused us by the foreigners, and based on my information he wrote his own proposals as to what should be done. Access to those buildings was impossible for everyone. So all I was able to do was to use the knowledge I gained from the ground, from intelligence, from what I would hear from individuals who encountered them, members of our brigade and others, and informed me later; and who were seeking a solution to the problem. These foreigners were not obeying anyone. They were only causing problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said they were not obeying anyone. Did you as a brigade have authority over them to issue orders?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that in my earlier testimony I have noted several times that we had no such authority. We never did, or even attempted it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to return to the beginning, Mr. Siljak, now. The only document we haven't seen is the information on the 306th Brigade, item number 1. The first document in the batch at the very beginning. Do you know what this decision is all about?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the wording of the oath that we received. Members of all units were supposed to take an oath and to sign the text of this oath.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After taking the oath, would they become members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I believe this happened after the proclamation of the state of war when the voluntary principle no longer applied. It was everyone's duty to defend and protect the state. After that, we received the text of the formal oath and we would apply this in our own units to members of the Territorial Defence who would be joining.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you in the 306th Brigade take care that this oath be followed by applying appropriate training, issuing cautions? Did you, in other words, try to make a real army out of those villagers?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The oath was taken by all the members who were in the units at the time. Later when new generations grew up and were conscripted, they took the oath in the units where they were mobilised. But throughout that, our main purpose was to familiarise them with the regulations of the army and the text of the oath was only one component of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were very calm and composed when you were describing all you went through in 1992 and 1993. But looking back from today's point of view, do you believe that the command of your brigade did everything in its capacity to create an army, defend its territory, and protect the population?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bearing in mind what exactly the command had at its disposal, and I mean primarily the commanding officers at brigade and unit level, and bearing in mind the materiel and equipment they had available to them as well as the high expectations they had of themselves and of everyone, I still don't believe that we could have done any more in terms of training and establishing the brigade as a unit. I believe that while I was in the 306th Brigade, the process of establishment of the brigade had not yet been completed. Later on I was a superior officer in the corps -- in the command of the 7th Corps. And I can say about the 306th Brigade that it never existed as a mountain brigade, probably because our ambitions at the time were exaggerated and we didn't know the situation well enough so we didn't make a very good assessment. That's why it had to be reformed from a 306th Mountain Brigade into a light infantry brigade, the difference being structural. And I still claim that up to the end of the war the 306th Mountain Brigade had not yet been established according to all the regulations and expectations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it because you didn't wish to do it or you didn't know how? Or the conditions in which you were acting were such that it was impossible?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our desire to achieve that was enormous, overwhelming; however the conditions wouldn't allow it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have completed my examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other Defence team may take the floor. The registrar will inform me of the length of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a very few specific questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Siljak I'll come back to a document you've seen. It's an interim report from May 1993; that is, Prosecution Exhibit P418, for the record.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at item 3.2. "Variant in case of attack by HVO unit." It says that: "Main forces of the 1st Battalion --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down when enumerating military units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: "Please mount an attack in the direction of Mehurici, Crni Vrh, Carda Kov, Guca Gora. Capture the line of attack from Maline, Radonjici, Krpeljici and Velika Bukovica," and so on.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This variant envisaged for the attack of HVO, was it ever implemented?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The axis mentioned in this variant was not implemented including the composition of forces that would be involved. So this variant was never actually used in our combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you clarify that the forces referred to in this variant, if I understood you correctly, were not all of them involved in the attack.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we did the planning how to use which forces in the territory from which the 306th Brigade took its replenishment, there is one company from the 314th Brigade from which the 306th Brigade took its replenishment. There is one company of the 314th Brigade from a battalion led by Midhat Puric. He was a native of Purici village. I showed it on the map. It was right next to the command post of the brigade. His unit took part on the 17th of April in the liberation of Stozerak hill, together with the 306th Brigade. So we were told that we should count on that unit when planning the use of forces, and we were also told at that moment that we should also envisage to use part of the forces of the 7th Muslim Brigade located then in Poculica. We were supposed to use them in combat activities effected at Vitez. And we were able to count on them because via this Stozerak hill in the interim territory, they could provide us with additional forces. However, we never came to implement this variant.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly in capturing the Maline-Radonjici- Krpeljici-Velika Bukovica line, the 7th Brigade did not take part.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did as far as I was informed. I was not present on that axis. But my operations officer said that only members -- in fact only units of the 306th Brigade were involved in that axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If we link up this document with your testimony today on page 26, lines 1, 2, 3, 4 when you said that towards Maline and Radonjici, and Guca Gora, free elements were advancing, you meant free elements of the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: We were talking today about the 8th of June. You said that free components were advancing towards Maline, Radonjici, Guca Gora. Did you mean free components of the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 306th Brigade that had been planned to intervene in case of an attack by the said Montenegrin aggressor. They were to advance towards the front line facing that aggressor and also go towards the axis facing the HVO in case the HVO attacked. These elements were made up of displaced population from Vakuf, Skender Vakuf, Kotor Varos, and similar places.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood you correctly, on that day members of the 7th Brigade did not advance along this axis.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I never said they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just one correction. On page 58, line 1, the record should display that they did not advance, contrary to what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the leave of the Chamber, could the witness approach the map to answer a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, we have ascertained that you are very familiar with this area around Travnik. Could you locate and mark on this map a locality called Hajdara fields.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have a trig point 681 marked on this map. Locals call it Hajdara fields. So at the eastern entrance to Travnik we see the Hajdara fields, and in this area while I was in the staff of the Territorial Defence anti-aircraft weapons of the HVO had already been deployed there and remained there until the clashes in June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the usher could help us and give a felt-tipped pen to Mr. Siljak so he can mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Just a little circle, please.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will actually fill it in to distinguish it from the rest of the marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You said you learned in June 1993. Did you say you learned of any combat operations in the area of Hajdara fields?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I didn't know anything. I was somewhere else. Shooting was heard in this area, but I had no information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you gain any knowledge later?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, later. But I can only tell you what I heard from others. The 1st Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade, which was in Travnik, apparently launched an attack on this feature, Hajdara fields at the same time as combat activities were taking place in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show us exactly how far is Hajdara fields from Travnik.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's just at the entrance into Travnik. So there was often fire against Dresje [phoen] and other buildings and features in town. If this is a map on the scale of 1:25.000, you can see that as the crow flies it's less than a kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Show us the road between Maline village and Hajdara fields.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What is the distance, do you know?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would make no sense to look at it as the crow flies because it seems too near, but the road between Hajdara fields and Maline would have to be winding. You would have to turn towards Guca Gora and then upwards via Travnik to Maline. So from Travnik to Guca Gora it's 9 kilometres, then another 3 kilometres to Maline, or more even. What is important is that there is something dividing these two places. If you look at the way positions were taken by the HVO. HVO took up position at Sveti Ivan Kotol and they opened fire constantly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please give him the red pen which he used to mark HVO positions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we used this colour to mark HVO. The red was for Serb positions. This is the colour we used for the HVO. Blue. Sorry, blue was for the army. So I was saying: Kotol. The HVO took up positions included Hajdara fields. At this time this part was impassable. They captured Grahova Glava, 1.600 metres high above the sea. Then we have Mala Bukovica; then comes Radonjici; and a pass that goes from Guca Gora linking up with Pokrajcici, this is the mountain pass; and only after that do we reach Maline. So this unit attacking here or the unit in Travnik in our assessment at the time was not reachable, could not provide us with any assistance. We could only count on the units below us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, they couldn't reach Maline at all.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: They couldn't, either in theory or in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, if this distance between Hajdara fields to Guca Gora is 9 kilometres by road and another 3 kilometres to Maline, that would be 12 kilometres in total.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, it's only my assessment. It's approximately 12 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: One more question, just one more, Mr. Siljak. When you were talking about Miletici, you said that you knew about Miletici through Mr. Ribo.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did Ribo mention that any unit of the BH army took part in that attack?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever I spoke to anybody from the command including Ribo, they only spoke of the Mujahedin. They didn't mention any unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did he or anyone else mention the presence of the 7th Brigade there?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no further questions for Mr. Siljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll have our break now. I'd like to ask the Prosecution how much time they will be needing, given that we will be resuming at about 5 to 1.00, which will leave us 45 minutes. Ms. Benjamin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I did indicate yesterday that we will probably be at least an hour, an hour and a half. And I think it looks more like an hour and a half now. So I think we may just be able to start the cross-examination, but we certainly won't be able to conclude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, as you have probably understood, it will be necessary for you to return on Tuesday afternoon. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving any interpretation, so I'm not sure what you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the Prosecution has just said that they will be needing an hour and a half. It appears -- we seem to be having a problem. Can you hear anything now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you put the volume up?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the volume be put up a little more, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution has just informed us that they will need an hour and a half to cross-examine you. The Judges will also have some questions to put to you. And after the Prosecution has cross-examined you, the Defence will probably want to ask you additional questions. This means that, unfortunately, you will have to return here on Tuesday afternoon. Is this a problem for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not a problem. I'll stay on as long as necessary for me to say what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will adjourn and resume at about 5 to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will now give the floor to Ms. Benjamin, who will start with cross-examination. And at 20 to 2.00, the registrar will take the floor to make the necessary corrections. Ms. Benjamin, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I just request that my volume be turned up, because it is only with great effort that I heard what was just said. I said right at the outset my hearing was not very good and I need the volume at the maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if the interpreters in their languages could speak up as well, maybe they could help the witness, too. All right, Ms. Benjamin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Siljak. My name is Tecla Henry-Benjamin. I am one of the Prosecutors representing the Prosecution in this matter and I wish, as Mr. President indicated earlier, to ask you a few questions concerning your testimony. If at any time I am going too fast or you don't understand anything I am saying, please feel free to stop me. You indicated to the Trial Chamber that you were born in Travnik and you gave us a guided tour of the whole Travnik area, which also included your area of responsibility. Could you please tell me, before the conflict, during the conflict, and after the conflict if it would be possible for you to have observed if there were other persons in the Travnik area other than inhabitants that you were accustomed to seeing.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood you well, I would just like to make one correction. In my testimony up to now, we encountered the area of responsibility facing the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor. So the zone of responsibility had two borders, the left and the right one, not in depth. Through my testimony I gave you a guided tour of the territory from which the 306th Brigade received its reinforcement, but there were other units there, too. That's the only thing I'd like to make clear. As for this specific question, I think I said earlier in my testimony that since I was an operations officer in the Main Staff but in charge of developments on the ground, somewhere in late spring, maybe in June actually, I noticed that foreign nationals were coming to Travnik, the press, humanitarian aid workers. And I noticed foreigners in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you. In your area of responsibility, could you state for the Trial Chamber which ethnic body, was the predominant body.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again I want to say that it was not our area of responsibility. The territory of Bila Valley was not the area of responsibility of the 306th Brigade. Instead, it was the territory from which we received reinforcements. I don't know if this is clear to you. We only got an area of responsibility assigned for particular operations we had to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. The area that you defined for us that you operated, the 306th -- we have the 306th Operative, that's the area I'm speaking about. That's the area I'm referring to. And my question to you is: Could you tell me which one, which ethnic body, was a majority in that area.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the north-east part of this territory, there was a majority Bosniak population. In the central area, the population was mixed. Nova Bila, Stara Bila, and that entire area was predominantly or entirely Croat. So if you take it as a whole, maybe there was a slight Bosniak prevalence over the Croats at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, your duties. In response to my learned friend you said amongst your duties, or rather that your main duty as chief of staff was to defend the line against the Serb aggressive forces. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first assignment the 306th Brigade received, its first mission, was to defend the line in the assigned zone of combat activities against the Serbian Montenegrin aggressor and to prepare active operations for the liberation of the temporarily occupied territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And I wish you to clarify for us then: What do you mean when you say "the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor"? What are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina it was a common term for the forces of the aggressor, namely the Serb forces aligned with the SDS from the Republika Srpska, remnants of the former JNA, and the volunteers from Montenegro. It was believed that the aggression against Bosnia and Herzegovina was carried out by Serbian Montenegrin forces. And that was the usual name used for them in the units in which I circulated.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I see. Chief of staff of the 306th Brigade. Did you see yourself responsible not only for defending the line but for defending all and sundry, everybody in your area of responsibility, whether it was civilians, military or otherwise? Did you see yourselves as performing that duty?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Travnik, there was a public security station. In other words, there was a police force in charge of controlling and protecting the territory. The 306th Brigade, therefore, was not responsible for the entire territory from which it received reinforcements.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. I have a problem with that, and I think I need to get it clarified. I'll do it by illustration of an example. If you were going down the main street in Travnik and you saw a civilian being attacked, do you think you were responsible to respond?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I personally should see somebody attacking a civilian, as a human being of course it would be my duty to help out. But as the chief of staff of the 306th Brigade, I had no such duty. My duty would possibly be to just report it to the nearest police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Are you saying then, or is it -- correct me if I'm wrong. Are you saying then that your responsibility was strictly to defend the line, and if you were to observe any illegal activities going on that you were to turn a blind eye? Would that be your instructions?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What sort of objection do you have to a question that makes sense?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has addressed the issue of the responsibility of the staff commander and brigade commanders. And before this question, he quite clearly answered my learned colleague's question, the same question. I think that this witness has answered the question three times and it's not necessary to confuse him in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The objection is denied. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: You see, I have a difficulty and I think to resolve it we need to get the correct answer to see what was the role of the BiH army, and in particular your role. You have indicated to us and in answer to my learned friend, and you just said it, at some point in time you saw an influx of foreigners coming in. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, I did notice them moving around, but I didn't mention the numbers. There were some of them there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And my question then, and that's why I tried to clarify it at first. Was that as a member of the army -- because in your evidence in-chief you said to my learned friend that these foreigners were committing crimes, they were uncontrollable, they were -- nobody was under anybody's command. Those were you words in evidence. And my question to you is: If this was taking place as you allege and you were a member of the army, don't you think that the onus was on you to deal with whoever or whatever was taking place in your AOR?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When answering the question about this matter, I said that we were involved in this issue right up until the point of time when the chief of security said that these acts had been committed by the Mujahedin who were not part of the 306th Brigade. So our responsibility consisted of the following: We were to investigate acts committed by members of our brigade, whereas at no point in time were the Mujahedin members of the 306th Brigade, not while I was in the brigade. And as far as I'm aware, neither afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, forgive me but I'm having a difficulty and that's why I'm trying to get it clarified. I cannot understand and tell me if you -- when you reason it out. I cannot understand. A war is going on or perhaps a conflict. You are the army; you're patrolling the area, you know, you are there to take care of the citizens and the inhabitants in your area. And here are a bunch of unruly, delinquent people turning a whole city upside down and terrorising everybody. Is it your evidence that the army, or your instructions were: Keep a blind eye. Only the front line; ignore everything. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President. My colleague's question contains the claim that the witness said that it was his duty to take care of the protection of the population. And this is not something that the citizen has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Benjamin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I didn't say the witness said that. I put it to him as an army member if he didn't think the onus was on him.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Can you answer, please.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the municipality of Travnik throughout the wartime period and before the war and during the wartime period, the civil political authorities were in function. There was the War Presidency of the Travnik municipality and they functioned within the municipality. And as for the control of the territory and the protection of the population, there was the Travnik police station and there were police stations in Turbe and two police stations in Travnik. There was also a police station in Mehurici. Their task was to control the territory and to protect the population in their area. The tasks of the BH army units and the tasks of the 306th was first and foremost to mount a defence against the enemy, that's what I already said, and then it was necessary to control and take care of acts perpetrated by subordinates, either by officers or by members of the units.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: When you were dealing with the Guca Gora segment, you indicated to my learned friend that there were times when you called on the military police for assistance. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say anything like that in the course of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Did you have to call on the military police for assistance?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: The 306th Brigade never worked along with the military police in any way?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I don't understand your question. The 306th Brigade had a military police platoon of its own.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Good. And you had to use them for assistance, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The officer responsible for suggesting that the MP platoon be used was the chief of security, or rather the assistant of the chief of security. The military police wasn't linked to the staff in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I understand that, but I'm saying to you that there were instances when, according to you, the chief of staff requested that the military platoon be used. Am I correct? There were times.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps you have misunderstood what I have said so far. I did attend meetings at which this was discussed, and I know about the military police being used in that manner. But I didn't request the assistance of the military police, not in my capacity as the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Okay. And maybe I should explain to you when I say "you," I don't necessarily mean you personally. The 306th Brigade. So there were times when the platoon of the 306th military were called out to assist. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I understand you better. I thought you were saying that I -- that you were referring to me as the chief of staff. But the 306th always used the military police unit that it had.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And that's the point we're getting to now. And you used them in Guca Gora with the burning and the looting. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: We used them in Guca Gora when it was necessary to provide security for the Guca Gora monastery. We also used them because that was in the immediate vicinity of the command post. We used them for the protection of the command post. They were used to control what members of the 306th Brigade's units were doing. In this case we were ordered to provide security for the Guca Gora monastery in order to protect it. And some military policemen were actually placed in the monastery itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: In hindsight now, do you think that it could have been possible that this same military patrol platoon could have been used in instances to control these unruly forces that patrolled the street? Do you think Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that that should have been possible?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, at that time -- well, I've tried to show you how complex the situation was in the area. The military police platoon was engaged at the forward command post of the 306th Brigade, which faced a Serbian aggressor. They were to provide security for the command post. Part of the military police were providing security for the monastery. Part of them were securing the command post and part of them, given the lack of men, were also engaged in combat operations. But in spite of that the police -- the military police weren't responsible for controlling civilians. And if the military police did go on patrol, it was its responsibility -- it was only to control and check up on members of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question for you at this point. I would like to ask the usher to show this document. It comes from the Defence. The number of the document is 704. This document comes from the Defence. Please read the document; it's an order from the 3rd Corps commander and it concerns the issue of civilian prisoners looting and destruction. You can see that in paragraph 1 it -- there is a request. Please read it out in your language. Read paragraph number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "In all units of the BH army in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps strictly forbid [as interpreted] the capturing of unarmed civilians, the looting of property, and the torching of facilities and infrastructure. Brigade commanders of municipal staffs and the offices at all levels of control and command shall take all possible measures to prevent those acts, and if this is not possible they shall make note of the events, register the perpetrators, and take the necessary measures to ensure that a disciplinary and penal sanctions are imposed on the perpetrators."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. And paragraph 2 that follows.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "In the event of looting or torching of unarmed civilians -- if looting, burning, or the taking of prisoner of unarmed civilians occurs and the competent officers do not take appropriate measures, the commanders of brigades and municipal defence staff shall be called to account. Instruct legal organs and units to punish such conduct and address it urgently in keeping with regulations and the law. Commanders of brigades and municipal staff shall issue their orders strictly forbidding these acts and shall take measures to ensure that all" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This order dated the 3rd of February, 1993. Was the 306th Brigade familiar with this order? Were you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I mentioned this order I said that we had received it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. When you received it and when we have a look at paragraph 1 and 2, should one draw the conclusion that naturally it is forbidden for anyone to imprison civilians, to damage their property -- to loot property or to damage it? And in paragraph 2 it seems to state that if a military or civilian authority failed, those in place should take the necessary measures. And that overlaps with the question that was just put to you. What sort of -- how do you interpret the official order that you received? Can we see individuals who were involved in looting or in other crimes? If that was the case, didn't the civilian or military authorities have the responsibility to act? That is what the order states. What conclusion would you draw on the basis of this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the first thing a soldier should do is to examine and understand the task when receiving such an order. And having examined this order, we came to the conclusion that this referred to members of units. We were responsible for unit members who committed such acts and on the basis of this order we were responsible for such things. And it was on this basis that we issued our order for all the units which were part of the 306th Brigade. But we weren't responsible for civilians. That wasn't within our remit. That was the responsibility of the civilian organs because there was a civilian -- there were civilian authorities and there was a BH MUP, or rather the Travnik police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But paragraph 2 seems to say, and this was drafted by the command of the 3rd Corps, it seems to say that if the responsible individuals take no action, others should take action. That's what it says. This order was sent to the military authorities, to the commands of brigades, and also to the civilian commanders -- to civilian authorities, because this is mentioned in the right-hand corner. This is not how you interpret the document. Very well. We take note of what you have said in that case. Usher, could you please take the document from the witness since it has been tendered into evidence. Please continue, Ms. Benjamin.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll give you the floor later.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: And Mr. Siljak, in fact I was just about to show you a document and it's in a similar vein to the one Mr. President has just shown you and it's Prosecution Exhibit 158/E. And it's an order from the commander. But what is of interest to me is the second line because it says: "During and after the comeback activities in your zone of responsibility, large-scale looting and burning of facilities belonging to the Croatian population has occurred. Such actions horrified the whole world and gave erroneous interpretation of our arms struggle." And the impression I get, Mr. Siljak, is that it was not only Croatian soldiers that he was referring to but all sundry, civilians, soldiers, everybody whose population has been destroyed, hence the reason why I asked the question earlier on. Because you see, destruction of property wasn't only done by one set of people, as you have said. There was a group of unruly people who were destroying. And my question again to you is: How did the 306th Brigade deal with it?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen this document before. This was a document to be delivered to the commander of the 306th Brigade command. As far as the use of military police is concerned, the commander dealt with these issues together with the chief of security or the assistant chief of security and with the military police of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HENRY-BENJAMIN
utterances.text: I believe that you haven't seen it but the point I was trying to make is the population -- the safety of the population is being considered. And that is the point I was trying to make to you. I really believe that you probably haven't seen it. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Benjamin, it's almost time. We need a few minutes to deal with the documents. Mr. Siljak, we will continue with the cross-examination next week and we'll have the Judges' questions and further questions from Defence counsel. I wish you a good stay here before returning to your country. Before you return, you shouldn't have any contact with anyone since you have taken the solemn declaration, you don't belong to either of the parties. We will see you on Tuesday again at the hearing that will start at 2.15. I will now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we have the corrections for the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'll try to be brief. So two comments. The first one concerns the French transcript. DH511, in the English version it was omitted yesterday. The English version will be DH511/E. DH1098, the English version is erroneous. DH1098/E; not DH10983/E. DH826 has been admitted, not DH821 which is what the transcript says. Naturally, the English version of this document is DH826/E. DH782 has been admitted, not DH582, and this affects the English version, too, which will be DH782/E. DH640; the English version 640/E and not DH643/E, as the transcript says. And in the French transcript, DH830 was omitted, it seems, and its English version is naturally DH830/E. And now for the English transcript: DH511. The English version doesn't the English version doesn't mention DH511, so it will be DH511/E. DH603 is in the transcript DH603/E, not DH603/1. DH613 is obviously DH613/E, not DH613 without anything afterwards as the transcript says. DH826 was tendered, not 821, which is what the transcript says. The English version is naturally affected, too, and it will be DH826/E. DH782 has been tendered into evidence, not DH582. And the English version will be 782/E. DH1044 has been tendered into evidence not DH104, which is what the transcript states. The English version is also affected, and tendered into evidence as DH1044/E. DH830, the English version is obviously DH830/E and not DH83/E, which is what the transcript says. And finally, DH582 was tendered into evidence, not 582 without DH. The English version is DH582/E. I have now finished, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I assume that Defence counsel will be requesting that all the documents be admitted into evidence. So, Mr. Registrar, you will have the weekend to work on the numbers for these documents and on Tuesday it will be our great pleasure to listen to you list the correct numbers. But you will have to take your time since as we realise errors were committed because of your speed of delivery. Yes, Ms. Residovic, you may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in view of the rules of this Tribunal and its jurisprudence according to which neither of the parties may contact the witness until the witness reappears before the Trial Chamber, but similarly, bearing in mind the practice of the Tribunal according to which with the assistance of the registry and the Victims and Witnesses Unit it might be possible for the witness to make an effort which might serve to tender documents into evidence. In view of all this Defence has spoken to the Prosecution. We would like to request that the Trial Chamber allow us to have the witness in the presence of representatives of the VWU and the registry, we would like -- and with the presence of the Prosecution and the Defence, we would like the witness to come to the courtroom so we can put a plastic map over this map and have the witness draw everything that he has already drawn on the map in permanent colours, because this can't be accepted as evidence since the colour gets defaced. This was the case in the Galic case and my colleagues from the Prosecution agree to this suggestion. Therefore we would be grateful if the Trial Chamber granted us leave to have the witness permanently mark what he has already marked on the map before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I have understood you correctly, the witness will be returning this afternoon and will use a plastic sheet, a transparent sheet, to once again draw what he has already drawn, and this will be in the presence of the registrar and the Prosecution. Mr. Mundis, have you agreed to this procedure?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We have indeed, Mr. President, but it wasn't my understanding it would be done this afternoon. We can certainly discuss, if the Trial Chamber agrees, with the registry VWS and the Defence as to the appropriate time and place where we can all be present to simply observe the witness doing this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Given that both parties agree on the procedure, it's necessary to obtain the witness's agreement, too. Perhaps he wants to go and ride his bicycle or something like that. But he should be informed that he is required to return this afternoon. As far as the Chamber is concerned, we don't object to the witness coming back to the courtroom in your presence, in the presence of the parties you have mentioned. This would -- this procedure would be forbidden if only one party came with the witness in order to make these amendments. But in this case, it's just a matter of making everything clearer and more precise. It is not a problem. I would like to thank you, and after this extended weekend I will see everyone back in the courtroom on Tuesday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 26th day of October, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.
